title: Vision of the New Temple (Measurements Begin)

questions.question: In what year of the exile did Ezekiel receive the visions of God that took him to the land of Israel (which begins the long temple vision)?
options: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month
In the middle of the thirtieth year, on the fifth day
In the very first year of the exile
In the fiftieth year, the year of Jubilee
questions.correctAnswer: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:1 (ESV): "In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck down, on that very day, the hand of the Lord was upon me..."

questions.question: Where did the visions of God set Ezekiel down?
options: Upon a very high mountain, on which was a structure like a city to the south
In the valley of dry bones again
Inside the courts of Babylon's palace
questions.correctAnswer: Upon a very high mountain, on which was a structure like a city to the south
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:2 (ESV): "In visions of God he brought me to the land of Israel, and set me down on a very high mountain, on which was a structure like a city to the south."

questions.question: What did the man Ezekiel saw in the vision look like?
options: His appearance was like bronze, with a linen cord and a measuring reed in his hand
He wore a crown of gold and royal purple
He had six wings and eyes all around
He looked like the Ancient of Days with white hair
questions.correctAnswer: His appearance was like bronze, with a linen cord and a measuring reed in his hand
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:3 (ESV): "When he brought me there, behold, there was a man whose appearance was like bronze, with a linen cord and a measuring reed in his hand. And he was standing in the gateway."

questions.question: What did the man in the vision command Ezekiel to do?
options: "Look with your eyes, and hear with your ears, and set your heart upon all that I shall show you... Declare all that you see to the house of Israel."
"Write these measurements in a scroll and seal it till the end of days."
"Speak to this mountain to move it to the sea."
"Measure the temple, but leave the outer court unmeasured."
questions.correctAnswer: "Look with your eyes, and hear with your ears, and set your heart upon all that I shall show you... Declare all that you see to the house of Israel."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:4 (ESV): "And the man said to me, 'Son of man, look with your eyes, and hear with your ears, and set your heart upon all that I shall show you... Declare all that you see to the house of Israel.'"

questions.question: What was the length of the man's measuring reed?
options: Six long cubits, each being a cubit and a handbreadth in length
Three spans of a man's hand
questions.correctAnswer: Six long cubits, each being a cubit and a handbreadth in length
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:5 (ESV): "And the man's measuring reed was six long cubits, each being a cubit and a handbreadth in length."

questions.question: The man first details a wall on the outside of the temple area, going all around it. What were its dimensions?
options: It was one reed thick, and one reed high
It was twelve cubits high and one cubit thick
It was as high as the clouds
There was no wall, only an open court
questions.correctAnswer: It was one reed thick, and one reed high
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:5 (ESV): "So he measured the thickness of the wall, one reed; and the height, one reed."

questions.question: Which gate did the man measure first?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:6 (ESV): "Then he went into the gateway facing east, going up its steps, and measured the threshold of the gate, one reed deep..."

questions.question: Inside the gateway, there were guardrooms on either side. How many guardrooms were there on each side of the east gateway?
options: One large one on either side
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:10 (ESV): "And there were three guardrooms on either side of the east gate. The three were of the same size..."

questions.question: What decorative carvings were on the jambs of the gateways?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:16 (ESV): "And there were narrow windows... And on the jambs were palm trees." (This is repeated throughout the gate descriptions).

questions.question: How many steps led up to the outer gateways (facing north, south, and east)?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:22, 26 (ESV): "And its windows, its vestibule, and its palm trees were of the same size as those of the gate that faced toward the east. And by seven steps people would go up to it..."

questions.question: After guiding Ezekiel through the outer court, the man brought him to the inner court gates. How many steps led up to the inner court gates?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:31, 34, 37 (ESV): "Its vestibule faced the outer court, and palm trees were on its jambs, and its stairway had eight steps." (The outer gates had seven, the inner had eight).

questions.question: What was placed in the vestibule of the inner gate, where the offering was to be slaughtered?
options: Four tables of hewn stone (two on one side, two on the other)
questions.correctAnswer: Four tables of hewn stone (two on one side, two on the other)
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:39 (ESV): "And in the vestibule of the gate were two tables on either side, on which the burnt offering and the sin offering and the guilt offering were to be slaughtered." (And v41: "Four tables were on the inside, and four tables on the outside... a total of eight tables").

questions.question: What were the tables of hewn stone meant for?
options: Slaughtering the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering
questions.correctAnswer: Slaughtering the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:39 (ESV): "to be slaughtered." And 40:42 "there were four tables of hewn stone for the burnt offering..."

questions.question: Inside the inner court, there were two chambers for the singers. Who were the chambers for the priests dedicated to?
options: One for the priests who keep charge of the temple, one for the priests who keep charge of the altar (the sons of Zadok)
One for the High Priest, one for the prophet
One for the Levites, one for the singers
One for the King, one for the priests
questions.correctAnswer: One for the priests who keep charge of the temple, one for the priests who keep charge of the altar (the sons of Zadok)
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:45-46 (ESV): "This chamber that faces south is for the priests who have charge of the temple, and the chamber that faces north is for the priests who have charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who alone among the sons of Levi may come near to the Lord to minister to him."

questions.question: Who alone among the sons of Levi may come near to the Lord to minister to Him?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 40:46 (ESV): "These are the sons of Zadok, who alone among the sons of Levi may come near to the Lord to minister to him."

key_verse_text: "And the man said to me, 'Son of man, look with your eyes, and hear with your ears, and set your heart upon all that I shall show you, for you were brought here in order that I might show it to you. Declare all that you see to the house of Israel.'"
